transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Well, I suppose the main reason I'm here is that my wife thinks I'm not eating enough. Most days I just have some coffee and a piece of toast in the morning, and then maybe a little soup or some vegetables later on. I just don't really see the issue. Big meals just feel completely unnecessary at my age.
Do you intentionally limit your food intake?

Well, like I was just saying, I do stick to just the coffee and toast, and maybe that little bit of soup or vegetables. I suppose it is intentional, yes. I make a point to keep my portions like that because... well, I just really don't need a lot of food at my age. So, yes, I do limit it on purpose, but it just makes sense to me to eat that way.
Have you lost any weight recently?

Well, yes, I suppose I have. My regular doctor actually told me recently that the number on the scale has gotten too low. But honestly, I don't see it as a bad thing. Being a bit lighter just makes it easier for me to get around. It's much easier to work out in the garden and keep up on my walks when I'm not carrying around extra weight. So I really don't mind it.
Do you think you are at a healthy weight right now?

Yes, I do. I honestly don't really see why everyone is making such a fuss about my weight. I mean... older folks are just supposed to eat less, aren't we? It's natural. And I'm still managing all my chores around the house, keeping up with my walks and everything without any trouble. So as far as I'm concerned, I'm doing just fine.
Do you think your weight is the same as it was when you were healthier?

I'm not exactly sure what you mean by when I was healthier. I mean... I feel healthy right now. I don't really remember what the scale used to say years ago, if that's what you're asking. I haven't really kept track of it to compare. I just know I feel fine the way I am today.
Do you think there's anything wrong with your body shape or size?

Well, I wouldn't use the word wrong, exactly. But I do pay attention to it. I mean... if I put my trousers on and my belt feels a notch looser, I feel like I've done right by myself. It's a good feeling. 

But on the other hand, if I look in the mirror and my stomach looks the least bit rounded... well, I feel sloppy. It's just disappointing. I just like to keep myself looking neat and trim, that's all.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Yes, I suppose I am. Well... when my wife tries to put butter on things, or if she serves me a full plate for dinner, I do get nervous. I just worry that I'll start putting weight back on. I've worked to keep things under control, and... I just don't want to lose that control.
Do you think you would still limit your food intake if you weren't trying to maintain your current weight?

I don't really know how to answer that. I mean... I am trying to maintain my weight, so that's why I do it. I haven't really thought about what I'd do if I wasn't. I just know that right now, keeping my portions small is what makes sense to me.
Do you think you would be upset if you gained a small amount of weight?

Yes, I would be. Like I mentioned a moment ago, it really makes me anxious when my wife tries to add butter to my food or gives me a full plate. I just get this nervous feeling that I'll start gaining the weight back. I've worked hard to keep things under control, and even a small amount of weight gain would feel like I'm losing that control.
Is your goal to be as thin as possible?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean... I'm not trying to waste away or see how thin I can get. I just want to stay exactly where I am right now. It's really just about not gaining the weight back and keeping things under control, rather than trying to lose more and more.
Do you feel like you would lose control if you stopped limiting your food intake?

Yes, I do. Like I was just saying about my wife... when she tries to give me those full plates or put butter on my food, if I just ate it all and stopped being careful, I'd definitely feel like I was losing my grip on things. It just makes me too nervous that the weight will come right back if I stop keeping an eye on it, and I'd lose all that control I've worked so hard to keep.
Do you think you would still want to limit your food intake if you didn't have concerns about gaining weight?

Well, I'm not really sure. I haven't really thought about it like that. I mean, the whole reason I watch my portions so closely is specifically because I don't want to gain the weight back. 

If I didn't have that worry hanging over me... I guess I probably wouldn't feel the need to be so strict about what I eat. I'd probably just eat whatever my wife puts in front of me. But it's hard to say for sure, since that concern is pretty much always there.
Is your main reason for limiting food intake to avoid gaining weight or to feel more in control of your body?

Well, I think they kind of go together. Like I was saying before, when my wife tries to put butter on things or hands me a full plate, I just get really nervous that I'll start putting the weight back on. And if I gain it back, then I lose that control I've worked so hard to keep. So... I guess the fear of gaining the weight is really what drives the need to keep things under control.
Is avoiding weight gain the main reason you limit your food intake, rather than feeling in control of your body being the main reason?

Yeah, that's exactly what I was just getting at. It really comes down to the weight. Like I said, when my wife tries to put butter on things or serves me a full plate, I just get so nervous that I'll start putting the weight back on. And if I do that, then I lose the control I've worked so hard to keep. So, yes, avoiding the weight is definitely the main reason.
Is there anything besides the fear of gaining weight that motivates you to limit your food intake?

No, not really. I... I can't think of anything else. It really just boils down to not wanting to put those pounds back on. If it weren't for that, I wouldn't have any reason to be so careful about what I'm eating. So, no, it's pretty much just the weight.
Do you feel like limiting your food intake is more about being in control or more about not gaining weight?

I... well, like I was just saying, Doc, it's definitely about not gaining the weight. I know I keep repeating myself here, but it really just goes back to what happens when my wife tries to put butter on my meals or hands me a full plate. That just makes me nervous that I'm going to start putting the weight back on. And if I gain it, then I lose the control I've worked so hard to keep. So, yes, avoiding the weight gain is the main thing.
Is there a specific body shape or weight that you are trying to maintain?

Well, I don't know if there's an exact number on the scale I'm aiming for, but... I definitely go by how I look and how my clothes fit. Like, if my belt feels a notch looser, I feel like I've done right by myself. It means I'm keeping things in check. But... if I look in the mirror and my stomach looks the least bit rounded, I just feel sloppy. I get really disappointed in myself. So I guess I'm just trying to keep my stomach flat and my clothes loose.
Would you say that your fear of gaining weight is the primary driver of your decision to limit your food intake?

Well, yes, I would. I know I've said it a couple of times now, but... yeah, that's exactly it. Not wanting to put those pounds back on is the main reason I do it. If I wasn't so worried about that, I wouldn't be so strict with my meals. So, yes, that's the primary thing driving it.
Do you think you would still want to be thinner even if you weren't afraid of gaining weight?

I... I'm not really sure how to answer that, Doc. I haven't really thought about it like that. I just know I don't want to gain the weight back. I don't know if it's about wanting to be thinner, exactly, or just... just wanting things to stay the way they are right now. I just want to keep the weight off.
Would you still try to lose weight if you weren't afraid of gaining weight?

Well, like I was just saying a minute ago... I really don't know. It's hard to separate all that in my head. The fear of putting the pounds back on is just always there, so... trying to imagine what I'd do if I wasn't afraid of it, I just don't have a good answer for you. I really couldn't say.
